subject: Proof-of-delete workflow for VPC with customer-owned object store

Subject: Deletion proof and chain-of-custody for our private VPC deployment

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Atlas is moving toward a private VPC deployment using a customer-owned S3 bucket in our AWS account. Before we sign the contract we need to understand how Redwood will support our retention and deletion obligations. Specifically: 

1) When we request tenant-level deletion, what controls does Atlas have to trigger and verify the wipe of objects retained inside our customer-owned bucket vs. any intermediate caches or logs?
2) Can Redwood provide a machine-readable proof-of-delete (hashes/timestamps) for objects you confirm removed?
3) What chain-of-custody evidence can you provide for forensics and audit (who performed the action, when, and the commands used)?

Attaching a short template of the deletion form our Security Ops wants completed. Also looping in legal.

Appreciate a short Q&A or delta to the standard SOW so we can move ahead.

Regards,
Susan
Director, Cloud Ops
Atlas Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Legal - Atlas Health <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Oct 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deletion proof and chain-of-custody for our private VPC deployment

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. I outlined answers below and included proposed operational steps to make verification reproducible for audit. Short version: for customer-owned object stores we operate under a customer-controlled flow: Redwood never writes primary customer data into our managed object storage, we hold ephemeral caches and logs that we can delete and attest. Full details and evidence examples below.

High-level answers:
- Trigger: Atlas can initiate via the console API or via the signed deletion-request-form (attached) sent to support.
- Proof-of-delete: We generate signed manifests (SHA256 hashes + timestamp + signer id) for each deletion job and bundle them into a tamper-evident archive.
- Chain-of-custody: Every deletion job is recorded in our audit log with operator id (service account or engineer), job id, parameters, and a reference to the manifest. We can export these logs for your auditors or provide a signed attestation.

Operational playbook (proposed):
1) Atlas opens a deletion request (console or the PDF).
2) Redwood validates request ownership and schedules a deletion job against the customer-owned bucket (we only issue S3 DeleteObjects using the AWS role you've granted).
3) Runtime garbage-collection runs to evict KV cache and ephemeral worker caches; we run a consistency pass to ensure no residual in-memory references.
4) Deletion job produces a manifest: list of object keys deleted, per-object SHA256, deletion timestamp, job id, executor id. The manifest is signed by Redwood's KMS key and returned to Atlas.
5) We publish a job-level audit record and optionally a PDF attestation signed by our compliance team.

I'll let Evelyn add details on evidence formats and Rishi on retention of audit logs and retention windows. If this looks good we'll convert the playbook to an SOW exhibit.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Deletion proof and chain-of-custody for our private VPC deployment

Susan / Ben — adding evidence and technical specifics. I work on Product Security and run our VPC deploy checks.

Evidence we can provide (examples):
- Signed manifest (JSON): {job_id, deleted_keys[], per_key_sha256[], deletion_time, signer: redwood-kms-key-arn, signature}.
- Job audit export (CSV): job_id, initiator_email, aws_role_used, API_calls_count, start_time, end_time, status.
- Optional object-level tombstone summary (for very large deletes we'll provide ranges and sampling).
- Hash-chain attestation: we can produce a chained-merkle root for the manifest set and sign it daily so auditors can verify manifest integrity over time.

About caches: we make a distinction between: (a) customer-owned objects in your bucket (we issue deletes and confirm via S3 headObject failures after deletion), and (b) transient inference artifacts (KV cache, prefix caches) stored on worker local NVMe. We do not persist those to your S3. For (b) we run a scrub after deletion jobs and report status; those scrubs are part of the manifest as non-object items with scrub checksums.

Format options: if Atlas prefers a machine-readable JSON manifest delivered to a pre-signed Atlas endpoint (S3 or HTTPS webhook), we can do that. Alternatively we can upload the signed manifest into a customer-controlled evidence folder in your S3 account if you prefer.

I'll coordinate with Engineering to add the manifest format and a sample.

Evelyn
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Deletion proof and chain-of-custody for our private VPC deployment

Susan — technical follow-up on retention windows and logs.

Retention defaults: For Private/VPC we permit customer-configured retention policies per-tenant. By default we retain audit logs for 90 days in our control plane. For customers with compliance needs we offer extended retention (1 year / 3 years) as a paid option. Audit logs include the deletion job record, API calls, and the manifest reference.

About proof-of-delete verification:
- After the deletion job completes we perform: HEAD on the object key to assert NotFound. We record the transient HTTP response code, timestamp, and the S3 request-id in the manifest.
- We also perform a sampling pass (configurable) over a percentage of deleted prefixes and store the sampling results in the manifest to avoid an expensive full-namespace walk on very large buckets.

For attestations: we can provide a signed attestation PDF (signed by compliance) that references the job id and includes hashes and the S3 request-ids. If you need per-object notarization, that is doable but will add cost and time.

Operational note: if Atlas prefers to run the final verification step themselves, we can provide a pre-signed list of deleted keys and a short-lived role you can assume to run a headObject sampling job. That puts the final verification in your hands and reduces coordinated evidence handling.

I'll follow up with the ops checklist and the exact log fields we can export.

Rishi

Redwood Inference
